key_insight: Beacon reframes agentic visual reasoning as a question of when to use tools and how to use them effectively, aiming to improve task success rather than just making reasoning more complex. It highlights that multimodal models need both tool-use awareness and better tool-effect choices.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the inefficiency of current agentic visual reasoning in multimodal large language models, where models may overuse tools, use them at the wrong time, or choose ineffective tools, reducing real-world task success.
method: Introduces two dimensions for evaluating tool use in MLLMs: Mode Adaptiveness (knowing when tools are necessary) and Tool Effect (choosing the right tool behavior).
Reframes agentic visual reasoning around success-oriented tool use rather than reasoning complexity alone.
Uses these dimensions to analyze and guide more efficient, task-effective multimodal reasoning.
impact: This matters because practitioners can build multimodal agents that are smarter about tool invocation, reducing wasted computation and improving reliability on complex visual tasks. It provides a clearer framework for designing and evaluating agentic MLLMs in practice.

paper_title: Beacon: Knowing When and How to Perform Agentic Visual Reasoning
paper_authors: Qixun Wang, Yang Shi, Letian Cheng, Zhuoran Zhang, Yan He
